mechanism_narrative: Increasing GDP indicates strong economic activity, leading to higher S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: 20-day returns do not increase when GDP growth is positive.

mechanism_narrative: Rising unemployment above 4% signals economic weakness, leading to negative S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: 20-day returns remain positive when unemployment exceeds 4%.

mechanism_narrative: High FEDFUNDS and low UNRATE indicate tight monetary policy, leading to negative S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: 20-day returns do not decrease when conditions are met.

mechanism_narrative: High inflation and employment growth signal wage pressures, leading to negative S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: 20-day returns do not decrease when conditions are met.

mechanism_narrative: Increasing housing starts indicate economic growth, leading to positive S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: 20-day returns do not increase with rising housing starts.

mechanism_narrative: Industrial production growth above 2% signals strong supply, leading to positive S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: 20-day returns do not increase with production growth.

mechanism_narrative: Low FEDFUNDS in easing cycles predict positive S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: 20-day returns are not higher during easing periods.

mechanism_narrative: Rising real consumption indicates strong demand, leading to positive S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: 20-day returns do not increase with rising consumption.
